title: The elect enter the holy place — no sorrow, plague, or torment
summary_md: When the tree is carried to the temple, Enoch is told what becomes of the righteous who eat of it: *Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:6). The prophets give the elect that same homecoming. Isaiah sees the ransomed come back to the mountain with the sorrow gone out of them: *the ransomed of Yahuah (LORD) shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away* (Isaiah 35:10), and he says why: *He will swallow up death in victory; and Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) will wipe away tears from off all faces* (Isaiah 25:8). It is the servants who eat in that day, and the division is plain in the same breath: *Behold, my servants shall eat, but ye shall be hungry... behold, my servants shall rejoice, but ye shall be ashamed* (Isaiah 65:13). Those who enter the holy place and those shut out of it are two companies, and the Father is the one who knows which is which. John closes the library on the same scene Enoch opened, with nothing left to touch them: *And Elohim (God) shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away* (Revelation 21:4).
note: old quote was 25:6 cited as 27:9; re-cited and re-quoted in full, canon witnesses kept

title: Water gushing in the desert — the wilderness made glad
summary_md: Enoch goes east into the mountains of the desert and finds the dry place alive: *And thence I went towards the east, into the midst of the mountain range of the desert, and I saw a wilderness and it was solitary, full of trees and plants. And water gushed forth from above. Rushing like a copious watercourse [which flowed] towards the north- west it caused clouds and dew to ascend on every side.* (1 Enoch 28:1-3). Farther on he comes to the valley itself: *And beyond these, I went afar to the east, and I saw another place, a valley (full) of water. And therein there was a tree, the colour (?) of fragrant trees such as the mastic.* (1 Enoch 30:1-2). This is the prophets' watered wilderness, the sign that Yahuah (LORD) has come to save His people: *The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.* (Isaiah 35:1), *for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert.* (Isaiah 35:6). The same hand that opens the water also plants the fragrant trees Enoch walks among: *I will open rivers in high places, and fountains in the midst of the valleys: I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.* (Isaiah 41:18) — *I will plant in the wilderness the cedar, the shittah tree, and the myrtle, and the oil tree; I will set in the desert the fir tree, and the pine, and the box tree together* (Isaiah 41:19), and the purpose is that all may *know, and consider, and understand together, that the hand of Yahuah (LORD) hath done this, and the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel) hath created it.* (Isaiah 41:20). Enoch walks the renewed desert the prophets sing about, and he walks it before they sang.
note: 28:5 (mastic tree, clusters of the vine) was not in Charles; the live 28:1-3 and 30:1-2 carry the watered wilderness; title adjusted to the live words

title: The tree no mortal may touch — the tree of life kept for the elect
summary_md: Michael tells Enoch what the fragrant tree is for: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy.* (1 Enoch 25:4) — *Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:5). This is the tree of life of Eden, planted and then guarded: *the tree of life also in the midst of the garden* (Genesis 2:9), barred from fallen hands *lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever* (Genesis 3:22), so that Yahuah *placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.* (Genesis 3:24). Enoch sees the same tree kept until the great judgement and then given to the righteous, and that is the very promise the risen Messiah holds out to the assemblies: *To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God).* (Revelation 2:7), and *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.* (Revelation 22:14). Notice who is given the fruit in both books. It is the commandment-keepers, the elect who keep the way, and never a class that chose itself. Ezekiel saw the same temple-fed fruit by the river from the sanctuary: *and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.* (Ezekiel 47:12). The tree fenced in Eden and opened again in Revelation is the tree Enoch already saw carried to the temple of the Eternal King.
note: quotes were 25:4-5 cited as 28:11-12; re-cited from the live verses; canon kept

title: The mountain whose summit is like the throne — seen on the way, named at the tree
summary_md: The throne-mountain is shown to Enoch before it is ever explained to him. On the earlier road he passes the seven mountains of stone and sees the middle one reach up: *But the middle one reached to heaven like the throne of Elohim (God), of alabaster, and the summit of the throne was of sapphire.* (1 Enoch 18:8). Then he comes to it again from the other side, and this time the tree stands in front of it: *And the seventh mountain was in the midst of these, and it excelled them in height, resembling the seat of a throne: and fragrant trees encircled the throne.* (1 Enoch 24:3). Only when he asks about the tree does Michael name the mountain: *And he answered saying: ‘This high mountain which thou hast seen, whose summit is like the throne of Elohim (God), is His throne, where the Holy Great One, Yahuah (Lord) of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.* (1 Enoch 25:3). So the mountain Enoch saw twice is one mountain, the seat the King will take when He comes down, and the fragrant tree belongs to it. John is shown the same throne with the same tree beside it at the end of the library: *And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of Elohim (God) and of the Lamb.* (Revelation 22:1), *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life... and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2). The throne, the tree, and the King who comes down to visit the earth are one vision, and it was carried whole from Enoch into the Apocalypse.
note: old summary built a 27:6-8 / 28:10 repetition that does not exist in Charles; the real repetition is 18:8 / 24:3 / 25:3; title changed to fit

title: The throne-mountain where the Eternal King comes down
summary_md: Michael answers Enoch's wonder at the tree by first naming the mountain it grows on: *And he answered saying: ‘This high mountain which thou hast seen, whose summit is like the throne of Elohim (God), is His throne, where the Holy Great One, Yahuah (Lord) of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.* (1 Enoch 25:3). The place of the throne is the place of the tree, and the King is coming down to it. Enoch had already seen that summit from the road, before the tree was in view: *And the seventh mountain was in the midst of these, and it excelled them in height, resembling the seat of a throne: and fragrant trees encircled the throne.* (1 Enoch 24:3). And the tree it keeps is the one set in Eden and then fenced from mortal hands: *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:* (Genesis 3:22). What Adam was barred from, the throne-mountain holds until the King comes down to visit the earth with goodness. The prophets put the same mountain at the centre of the last days: *And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD’S house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.* (Isaiah 2:2). It ain't new. Enoch was shown the seat before Isaiah saw the house built on it.
note: old summary cited a 24:9 / 29:9 repetition that is not in Charles and called it "the framework's Zion-centre"; rebuilt on 25:3 / 24:3 with Isaiah 2:2 added from the verse index

title: The tree of life kept until the great judgement, food for the elect
summary_md: The fragrant tree is no ordinary tree, and Michael says so: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy. Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:4-5). This is Eden's own tree, the one Yahuah planted *pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden* (Genesis 2:9), and then sealed from mortal reach so that no man should *take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever* (Genesis 3:22). Enoch sees the same fruit given back to the elect at the end, and that is exactly the promise Yahusha (Jesus) makes to the overcomer: *To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God).* (Revelation 2:7). He shows it again standing in the City: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2). Ezekiel saw it too, growing by the water that comes out from under the sanctuary: *And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.* (Ezekiel 47:12). The tree withheld since Eden is the tree given to the righteous after the judgement, and the holy place is where it is given.
note: old 29:10-11 was a paraphrase of 25:4-5 from the corrupt text; re-quoted from the live verses in full; canon kept

title: Transplanted to the temple: long life and no more sorrow
summary_md: The tree's destiny is the sanctuary, and the destiny of the elect is life beside it: *Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King. Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:5-6). This is the prophets' restored earth, where the days of the people are measured like the days of a tree: *They shall not build, and another inhabit; they shall not plant, and another eat: for as the days of a tree are the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands.* (Isaiah 65:22). The end of sorrow and plague and torment that Enoch names is the same comfort the prophets and the Revelation give: *He will swallow up death in victory; and Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for Yahuah (LORD) hath spoken it.* (Isaiah 25:8), unfolded at the end as *And Elohim (God) shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.* (Revelation 21:4). The right to enter the holy place and eat is kept for those who keep the way: *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.* (Revelation 22:14). Enoch says the fathers lived such a life once; the prophets say the elect will live it again.
note: old 29:11-12 was 25:5-6 under the wrong number; re-cited and quoted in full

title: The fragrant trees of the east — the chief spices
summary_md: Past the valley of water Enoch walks through country that smells like the sanctuary: *And on the sides of those valleys I saw fragrant cinnamon. And beyond these I proceeded to the east.* (1 Enoch 30:3), then *And I saw other mountains, and amongst them were groves of trees, and there flowed forth from them nectar, which is named sarara and galbanum. And beyond these mountains I saw another mountain to the east of the ends of the earth, whereon were aloe-trees, and all the trees were full of stacte, being like almond-trees. And when one burnt it, it smelt sweeter than any fragrant odour.* (1 Enoch 31:1-3), and north of these, *And after these fragrant odours, as I looked towards the north over the mountains I saw seven mountains full of choice nard and fragrant trees and cinnamon and pepper.* (1 Enoch 32:1). Cinnamon, nectar, galbanum, stacte, aloes, nard — these are the spices Yahuah (LORD) set apart for His own house. The incense of the holy place is compounded from the same list: *Take unto thee sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; these sweet spices with pure frankincense: of each shall there be a like weight* (Exodus 30:34), and the anointing oil from the rest of it: *Take thou also unto thee principal spices, of pure myrrh five hundred shekels, and of sweet cinnamon half so much, even two hundred and fifty shekels, and of sweet calamus two hundred and fifty shekels,* (Exodus 30:23). The Song gathers them into the Bridegroom's garden: *Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:* (Song of Solomon 4:14). Enoch's eastern mountains are growing the very things the Torah later tells the priests to burn before Yahuah (LORD). The sanctuary smells like the garden because the garden came first.
note: old 30:1-2 quotes (styrax, onycha, balsam) are not in Charles; rebuilt on the live 30:3, 31:1-3, 32:1; canon kept, Exodus 30:34 added from the old 31 thread

title: The tree of wisdom — Eden's tree of knowledge
summary_md: At the Garden of Righteousness Enoch finds one tree set apart from the rest: *And I came to the Garden of Righteousness, and saw beyond those trees many large trees growing there and of goodly fragrance, large, very beautiful and glorious, and the tree of wisdom whereof they eat and know great wisdom. That tree is in height like the fir, and its leaves are like (those of) the Carob tree: and its fruit is like the clusters of the vine, very beautiful: and the fragrance of the tree penetrates afar.* (1 Enoch 32:3-4). He asks about it, and the angel names it: *Then Raphael the holy angel, who was with me, answered me and said: ‘This is the tree of wisdom, of which thy father old (in years) and thy aged mother, who were before thee, have eaten, and they learnt wisdom and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked and they were driven out of the garden.’* (1 Enoch 32:6). This is Eden's own tree, the one Genesis sets *in the midst of the garden*: *And out of the ground made Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.* (Genesis 2:9). Enoch's phrase *they learnt wisdom* is Eve's reach for it: *And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.* (Genesis 3:6). And *their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked* is the fall told in Moses' own words: *And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.* (Genesis 3:7). So is the driving out: *So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.* (Genesis 3:24). Raphael is reading Genesis 2 and 3 to Enoch, naming the tree of knowledge by its fruit and by what it cost, with the way back still guarded until the appointed day.
note: old 30:7 was 32:6 under the wrong number; re-cited, 32:3-4 added so the reader sees the tree before the naming

title: The tree transplanted to the temple — fruit for the righteous
summary_md: The tree withheld from Adam is not destroyed. It is kept: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy. Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King. Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:4-6). John sees the same tree replanted at the centre of the renewed city: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2), and only the covenant-keepers come to it: *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.* (Revelation 22:14). Ezekiel sets the same healing trees along the water that flows from the sanctuary: *And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.* (Ezekiel 47:12). The tree denied at the fall is carried to the temple-mountain at the judgement and its fruit goes to the elect who keep the way. That is a restoration of the covenant people at the centre, not a replacement of them, and Enoch saw it before Ezekiel or John did.
note: old quoted 30:8-10 and 24:11, none of which exist in Charles; the live 25:4-6 carries the whole thought; canon kept

title: The fragrant trees — frankincense and myrrh
summary_md: East of the mountain range Enoch comes to trees that breathe the incense of worship: *And thence I went to another place in the desert, and approached to the east of this mountain range. And there I saw aromatic trees exhaling the fragrance of frankincense and myrrh, and the trees also were similar to the almond tree.* (1 Enoch 29:1-2), and beyond them, *And beyond these mountains I saw another mountain to the east of the ends of the earth, whereon were aloe-trees, and all the trees were full of stacte, being like almond-trees. And when one burnt it, it smelt sweeter than any fragrant odour.* (1 Enoch 31:2-3). Frankincense and myrrh are the fragrances Yahuah (LORD) reserves for His sanctuary: *Take unto thee sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; these sweet spices with pure frankincense: of each shall there be a like weight* (Exodus 30:34). They are the same smoke that goes up around the Bridegroom as He comes out of the wilderness: *Who is this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?* (Song of Solomon 3:6). Enoch says that when the aloe was burnt it smelt sweeter than any fragrant odour, and that is a man describing incense before Moses was told how to compound it. The trees of the east were worship trees from the start.
note: old 31:1 and 31:3 are not in Charles; the live 29:1-2 and 31:2-3 carry frankincense, myrrh, and the burning; canon kept

title: The tree of wisdom — eyes opened, driven from the garden
summary_md: The angel names the tree for Enoch: *Then Raphael the holy angel, who was with me, answered me and said: ‘This is the tree of wisdom, of which thy father old (in years) and thy aged mother, who were before thee, have eaten, and they learnt wisdom and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked and they were driven out of the garden.’* (1 Enoch 32:6). This is Eden retold without a seam. Eve saw *a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof... and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat* (Genesis 3:6); then *the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked* (Genesis 3:7); and Yahuah Elohim *sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken* (Genesis 3:23). Enoch is shown the very tree Genesis names, standing where it stood, still bearing. The order Yahuah set in the garden was good; the fall was a reach for wisdom apart from the Creator's way, and the command that was broken was never the thing at fault.
note: old 31:4 was 32:6 under the wrong number; re-cited

title: The tree reserved for the elect — transplanted to the holy place
summary_md: The tree Michael shows Enoch is sealed off until the day of reckoning and then given back to the righteous: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy. Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:4-5). This is the Eden tree carried home to the mountain of the house. Ezekiel sees it rooted by the sanctuary stream: *shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed... because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine* (Ezekiel 47:12); Revelation sets it in the City: *the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits... and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations* (Revelation 22:2); and the way in is for those who keep the covenant: *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city* (Revelation 22:14). The vengeance falls on all who earned it, the fruit goes to the righteous and holy, and the tree is planted again at the centre. Eden, the mountain of the house, and the age to come are one story told three times.
note: old 31:5-6 were paraphrases of 25:4-5 under invented numbers; re-quoted from the live verses; canon kept

title: Driven out — the tree of wisdom and the way kept
summary_md: Of the tree their parents ate from Enoch is told the end of the matter: *Then Raphael the holy angel, who was with me, answered me and said: ‘This is the tree of wisdom, of which thy father old (in years) and thy aged mother, who were before thee, have eaten, and they learnt wisdom and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked and they were driven out of the garden.’* (1 Enoch 32:6). Genesis gives the reason for the driving out, that fallen man should not seize life for ever: *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever* (Genesis 3:22), and it names the guard set at the gate: *So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life* (Genesis 3:24). Enoch, standing in the Garden of Righteousness with the tree of wisdom in front of him, is being shown that the garden is still there and the way is still kept. What Raphael says of this tree matches what Michael said of the other: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy.* (1 Enoch 25:4). The bar was never on wisdom itself. It was on wisdom taken against the command, and the righteous wait for the great judgement, when the way is opened again.
note: old 32:6-7 ran the 32:6 words into a sentence Charles does not have; rebuilt on 32:6 with 25:4 beside it; Proverbs 3:18 dropped (not in the verse index)

title: The fruit given to the righteous — transplanted to the temple
summary_md: At the great judgement Enoch's tree is opened to the elect and moved to the holy place: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy. Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King. Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:4-6). A tree of Eden standing in a holy place is the prophets' own picture, because Eden was always the garden of Elohim (God): *Thou hast been in Eden the garden of Elohim (God); every precious stone was thy covering, the sardius, topaz, and the diamond, the beryl, the onyx, and the jasper, the sapphire, the emerald, and the carbuncle, and gold: the workmanship of thy tabrets and of thy pipes was prepared in thee in the day that thou wast created* (Ezekiel 28:13). Yahusha (Jesus) gives the same promise to the overcomer: *He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God)* (Revelation 2:7), and Revelation sets the tree at the throne in the holy city: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations* (Revelation 22:2), with its right reserved for the commandment-keepers: *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city* (Revelation 22:14). 2 Esdras hears the same opening: *For to you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, plenteousness is made ready, a city is builded, and rest is allowed, yes, perfect goodness and wisdom* (2 Esdras 8:52). The fruit is for the elect who keep the way, and the tree is carried to the temple of Yahuah (Lord) at the centre.
note: old 32:8-9 was 25:5-6 under the wrong number; re-quoted in full; canon kept

title: The stars come forth in their order — the courses Enoch wrote down
summary_md: At the eastern ends of the earth Enoch watches the host come out through its gates: *And to the east of those beasts I saw the ends of the earth whereon the heaven rests, and the portals of the heaven open. And I saw how the stars of heaven come forth, and I counted the portals out of which they proceed, and wrote down all their outlets, of each individual star by itself, according to their number and their names, their courses and their positions, and their times and their months, as Uriel the holy angel who was with me showed me.* (1 Enoch 33:2-3), and *He showed all things to me and wrote them down for me: also their names he wrote for me, and their laws and their companies.* (1 Enoch 33:4). The stars have courses and times and laws, and Uriel had them written. This is the lesson Enoch opens the whole book with: *Observe ye everything that takes place in the heaven, how they do not change their orbits, and the luminaries which are in the heaven, how they all rise and set in order each in its season, and transgress not against their appointed order.* (1 Enoch 2:1). He had already seen what turns them: *I saw the winds of heaven which turn and bring the circumference of the sun and all the stars to their setting.* (1 Enoch 18:4). The Tanakh reads the same fidelity in the heavens: *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.* (Psalm 104:19), and the Creator alone holds the reins of the constellations — *Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion?* (Job 38:31), *Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in his season? or canst thou guide Arcturus with his sons?* (Job 38:32). The stars that never break rank are Enoch's standing rebuke to the ones that did, for he was shown their prison on the same journey: *And the stars which roll over the fire are they which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (Lord) in the beginning of their rising, because they did not come forth at their appointed times.* (1 Enoch 18:15). The heavens keep the order they were given, and rebellion against the appointed courses is where the trouble began.
note: old 33:5 and 33:7 are not in Charles; the live 33:2-4, 18:4 and 18:15 carry the thought; canon kept

title: The great beasts and birds at the ends of the earth — the Creator's works kept
summary_md: Before Enoch reaches the gates of heaven he passes the creatures that live at the edge of the world: *And from thence I went to the ends of the earth and saw there great beasts, and each differed from the other; and (I saw) birds also differing in appearance and beauty and voice, the one differing from the other.* (1 Enoch 33:1). Then the gates: *And to the east of those beasts I saw the ends of the earth whereon the heaven rests, and the portals of the heaven open.* (1 Enoch 33:2). Every kind differs from every other kind, and Enoch counts them as he counts the stars, each one by itself. That is Genesis speaking, every creature after its kind, and the man set over them to name them. Enoch is doing the work Adam was given, writing down names and courses and kinds under an angel's instruction. The fragrant tree he had smelt on the throne-mountain belongs to the same ordered creation: *And amongst them was a tree such as I had never yet smelt, neither was any amongst them nor were others like it: it had a fragrance beyond all fragrance, and its leaves and blooms and wood wither not for ever: and its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit resembles the dates of a palm.* (1 Enoch 24:4). And the tree that wither not is the one Ezekiel sees by the sanctuary stream — *And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.* (Ezekiel 47:12) — and the one John is shown at the end: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2). What Enoch sees at the ends of the earth and what he smelt on the mountain are one creation, kept in order and kept for the righteous.
note: old 33:10 (trees of paradise at the north) is not in Charles 33; rebuilt on the live 33:1-2 with the 24:4 tree kept; Genesis 2:9 dropped since the live chapter has no paradise; title changed

title: The treasuries of the winds — He ordered all creation by His wisdom
summary_md: Enoch is shown where the winds are kept and what they do: *I saw the treasuries of all the winds: I saw how He had furnished with them the whole creation and the firm foundations of the earth. And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:1-2). At the ends of the earth he sees the gates they come through: *And here I saw three portals of heaven open in the heaven: through each of them proceed north winds: when they blow there is cold, hail, frost, snow, dew, and rain. And out of one portal they blow for good: but when they blow through the other two portals, it is with violence and affliction on the earth, and they blow with violence.* (1 Enoch 34:2-3). These are the very treasuries Yahuah (LORD) set before Job out of the whirlwind — *Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,* (Job 38:22) — and the prophets confess the wind drawn out of the same store: *He causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings for the rain; he bringeth the wind out of his treasuries.* (Psalm 135:7), *When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens, and he causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.* (Jeremiah 10:13). Jeremiah names the wisdom behind the store in the verse before: *He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heavens by his discretion.* (Jeremiah 10:12). The world is not loose. It is furnished, founded, and ordered by the One who weighs the snow and appoints the seasons, and Enoch saw the furnishing.
note: old 33:11-12 are not in Charles 33; the live 18:1-2 and 34:2-3 carry the treasuries; Proverbs 8:22 dropped (not in the index), Jeremiah 10:12 added from the index

title: The four winds that bear the earth — the four quarters
summary_md: Having walked north, east, south, and west, Enoch has seen the whole frame of the world at its corners, and on the earlier journey he had already seen what holds it: *And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:2). The four winds are a fixed feature of the prophets' visions. Daniel watches them stir the nations: *Daniel spake and said, I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sea.* (Daniel 7:2). John sees angels set over them, held back until the sealing is done: *And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.* (Revelation 7:1). Enoch's own book of the luminaries names the quarters one by one: *And the first quarter is called the east, because it is the first: and the second, the south, because the El Elyon (Most High) will descend there, yea, there in quite a special sense will He who is blessed for ever descend. And the west quarter is named the diminished, because there all the luminaries of the heaven wane and go down.* (1 Enoch 77:1-2). The earth ordered to four corners, with winds held or loosed at the Creator's word, is the architecture Daniel and John take for granted, and Enoch is the one who wrote it down first.
note: old 34:6 is not in Charles 34; the live 18:2 and 77:1-2 carry the four winds and quarters; canon kept

title: The winds that bear the earth — the pillars of heaven
summary_md: Enoch is shown the frame of the cosmos and what holds it up: *And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven. And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:2-3). The canon speaks the same architecture. Job knows both the hung earth and the trembling pillars: *He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.* (Job 26:7), *The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his reproof.* (Job 26:11). Isaiah sees the heavens stretched out like a tent — *It is he that sitteth upon the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers; that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in:* (Isaiah 40:22) — and the Psalm makes the very winds His servants: *Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire:* (Psalm 104:4). Enoch's pillars and stretched-out vaults are the picture the canon already carries, a heaven the Creator hangs, spreads, and upholds, with the winds standing at their station to do it.
note: old 34:7-8 were 18:2-3 under the wrong numbers; re-cited; canon kept

title: The west portals and the storehouses of wind, dew, and rain
summary_md: Enoch comes to the western edge and finds the same ordered gates he had seen in the east: *And from thence I went towards the west to the ends of the earth, and saw there three portals of the heaven open such as I had seen in the east, the same number of portals, and the same number of outlets.* (1 Enoch 35:1). What comes through such gates he had just been shown on the north side: *And here I saw three portals of heaven open in the heaven: through each of them proceed north winds: when they blow there is cold, hail, frost, snow, dew, and rain. And out of one portal they blow for good: but when they blow through the other two portals, it is with violence and affliction on the earth, and they blow with violence.* (1 Enoch 34:2-3), and on the south: *And from thence I went to the south to the ends of the earth, and saw there three open portals of the heaven: and thence there come dew, rain, and wind.* (1 Enoch 36:1). The wind comes as gift and as affliction, and both are sent, not loosed. The Tanakh already keeps wind and weather in named storehouses that Yahuah (LORD) opens at His word: *He causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings for the rain; he bringeth the wind out of his treasuries.* (Psalms 135:7); *When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens, and he causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.* (Jeremiah 10:13); and the same storehouses hold the frost and hail Enoch names — *Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,* (Job 38:22). This is the Creator's order, and Enoch is shown it gate by gate, so that the reader can tell it apart from the disorder the Watchers brought.
note: old 35:2 and 35:8 are not in Charles 35 (which has one verse); the live 34:2-3 and 36:1 carry the winds through the gates; canon kept

title: The four quarters of the earth and the four winds
summary_md: From the western edge Enoch has now seen all four sides of the world, and he had already been shown what divides it: *And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:2). The four winds and four quarters are the standard furniture of the prophets. Daniel watches them stir the nations: *Daniel spake and said, I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sea.* (Daniel 7:2). Zechariah is told the four chariot-spirits are the same: *And the angel answered and said unto me, These are the four spirits of the heavens, which go forth from standing before Yahuah (Lord) of all the earth.* (Zechariah 6:5). John sees them held back at the corners: *And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.* (Revelation 7:1). And Yahusha (Jesus) gathers the scattered seed from these same four winds at the end: *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31). The four quarters Enoch surveys are the compass the elect of Yashar'el (Israel) are gathered home from.
note: old 35:5 is not in Charles 35; the live 18:2 carries the four winds; canon kept

title: The pillars of heaven and the stretched-out firmament
summary_md: Enoch sees the winds themselves doing the structural work of holding the world up: *And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven. And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:2-3). The Tanakh names these pillars and the firmament they bear. Job knows the heavens rest on pillars that tremble at a word: *The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his reproof.* (Job 26:11), and Hannah sings that the earth's foundations are Yahuah's own setting: *He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the LORD'S, and he hath set the world upon them.* (1 Samuel 2:8). The firmament Enoch sees stretched is the firmament of the second day: *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.* (Genesis 1:6). And when the journey is over Enoch says plainly whose work it all is: *And as often as I saw I blessed always Yahuah (Lord) of Glory, and I continued to bless Yahuah (Lord) of Glory who has wrought great and glorious wonders, to show the greatness of His work to the angels and to spirits and to men, that they might praise His work and all His creation: that they might see the work of His might and praise the great work of His hands and bless Him for ever.* (1 Enoch 36:4). The whole survey is creation kept in the Creator's order, the opposite of the disorder the Watchers brought into it.
note: old 35:6-7 were 18:2-3 under the wrong numbers and 36:9 is not in Charles; re-cited, 36:4 quoted for the close; canon kept

title: The portals of heaven and the four winds
summary_md: Enoch finishes the circuit at the south and the east: *And from thence I went to the south to the ends of the earth, and saw there three open portals of the heaven: and thence there come dew, rain, and wind. And from thence I went to the east to the ends of the heaven, and saw here the three eastern portals of heaven open and small portals above them. Through each of these small portals pass the stars of heaven and run their course to the west on the path which is shown to them.* (1 Enoch 36:1-3). The stars run their course on a path that is shown to them, and the winds come through gates that are counted. John sees the same four-cornered order held in place in the last days: *And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.* (Revelation 7:1). Job already knew the winds are weighed by the Creator's hand — *To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure.* (Job 28:25) — and Enoch names the quarters himself in the book of the luminaries: *And the first quarter is called the east, because it is the first: and the second, the south, because the El Elyon (Most High) will descend there, yea, there in quite a special sense will He who is blessed for ever descend. And the west quarter is named the diminished, because there all the luminaries of the heaven wane and go down.* (1 Enoch 77:1-2). The four winds are servants under orders, not powers loose in the world.
note: old 36:1 and 36:3 are not in Charles; the live 36:1-3 carries the portals; 77:1 stood, 77:2 added to complete the quarters; canon kept

title: The winds that bear the earth — the pillars of heaven
summary_md: On the earlier road Enoch had been shown what the gates of the four winds serve: *I saw the treasuries of all the winds: I saw how He had furnished with them the whole creation and the firm foundations of the earth. And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven. And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:1-3). Scripture speaks the same way of the world resting on the Creator's pillars: *He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the LORD'S, and he hath set the world upon them.* (1 Samuel 2:8). The stretching-out of the heavens is the Creator's own act — *He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heavens by his discretion.* (Jeremiah 10:12) — and when Yahuah answers Job He puts the same foundation in front of him: *Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.* (Job 38:4). Enoch is not describing brute pillars. He is describing the ordered service of winds holding up what Yahuah founded, and at the end of the journey he blesses the One who founded it: *And as often as I saw I blessed always Yahuah (Lord) of Glory, and I continued to bless Yahuah (Lord) of Glory who has wrought great and glorious wonders, to show the greatness of His work to the angels and to spirits and to men, that they might praise His work and all His creation: that they might see the work of His might and praise the great work of His hands and bless Him for ever.* (1 Enoch 36:4).
note: old 36:4-5 were 18:2-3 under the wrong numbers; re-cited with 18:1 and 36:4 beside them; canon kept

title: All creation ordered by His wisdom — Enoch blesses Yahuah of glory
summary_md: The Book of the Watchers closes with Enoch blessing the Maker of everything he has just been shown: *And as often as I saw I blessed always Yahuah (Lord) of Glory, and I continued to bless Yahuah (Lord) of Glory who has wrought great and glorious wonders, to show the greatness of His work to the angels and to spirits and to men, that they might praise His work and all His creation: that they might see the work of His might and praise the great work of His hands and bless Him for ever.* (1 Enoch 36:4). The canon confesses the same thing in the same words. The world is made by wisdom — *He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heavens by his discretion.* (Jeremiah 10:12) — and its praise goes up from the whole circuit Enoch has just walked: *From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the LORD'S name is to be praised.* (Psalm 113:3). Jubilees confesses the same six-day ordering, that even *the angels of the spirit of the winds... and of snow and of hail and of hoar frost* (Jubilees 2:2) were created and set to serve. Enoch says the wonders were shown to angels and spirits and men so that they might praise, and that is the whole purpose of the journey. He ends the way every righteous one ends, blessing the Creator whose wisdom holds the world.
note: old 36:9 is not in Charles; the live 36:4 is the doxology; Proverbs 3:19, Psalm 104:24, 19:1-2, 148:3 dropped (not in the verse index), Jeremiah 10:12 added from it

title: The Holy Great One comes forth from His dwelling to tread the earth at Sinai
summary_md: Enoch's second vision is a vision of wisdom, and he says who it is for: *And this is the beginning of the words of wisdom which I lifted up my voice to speak and say to those which dwell on earth: Hear, ye men of old time, and see, ye that come after, the words of the Holy One which I will speak before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 37:2). Its substance is the same coming he had announced at the very opening of the book: *Concerning the elect I said, and took up my parable concerning them: The Holy Great One will come forth from His dwelling, And the eternal Elohim (God) will tread upon the earth, (even) on Mount Sinai, [And appear from His camp] And appear in the strength of His might from the heaven of heavens.* (1 Enoch 1:3-4). This is the Sinai-coming of the Torah and the prophets, word for word. Moses' blessing opens with it: *Yahuah (LORD) came from Sinai, and rose up from Seir unto them; he shined forth from mount Paran, and he came with ten thousands of saints: from his right hand went a fiery law for them* (Deuteronomy 33:2). Micah sees the same coming forth and treading: *For, behold, Yahuah (LORD) cometh forth out of his place, and will come down, and tread upon the high places of the earth* (Micah 1:3). And Jude lifts the judgement-coming straight off this book: *And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, Yahuah (Lord) cometh with ten thousands of his saints* (Jude 1:14). The One who comes forth here is the Holy Great One in His own might from the heaven of heavens; the Elect One who sits on the throne of glory is not named until the parables reach chapters 46 and 48, and the book keeps that order on purpose. Enoch's Sinai is Moses' Sinai and Micah's, and the men of old time and those who come after are told to hear it together.
note: old 37:5-6 was 1:3-4 under the wrong numbers; re-cited; "the framework keeps" removed; 37:2 quoted to tie the parable to the advent; canon kept

title: The mountains melt like wax; the earth is rent; judgement upon all
summary_md: Before His presence the whole created order gives way, and judgement falls: *And all shall be smitten with fear, And the Watchers shall quake, And great fear and trembling shall seize them unto the ends of the earth. And the high mountains shall be shaken, And the high hills shall be made low, And shall melt like wax before the flame. And the earth shall be wholly rent in sunder, And all that is upon the earth shall perish, And there shall be a judgement upon all (men).* (1 Enoch 1:5-7). Micah carries the melting mountains straight on from the Sinai-advent: *And the mountains shall be molten under him, and the valleys shall be cleft, as wax before the fire, and as the waters that are poured down a steep place* (Micah 1:4). Nahum names the same quaking and burning at His presence: *The mountains quake at him, and the hills melt, and the earth is burned at his presence, yea, the world, and all that dwell therein* (Nahum 1:5), and Isaiah cries out for the very rending Enoch foresees: *Oh that thou wouldest rend the heavens, that thou wouldest come down, that the mountains might flow down at thy presence* (Isaiah 64:1). That the Watchers themselves quake ties this judgement to the war of the seed that this book carries forward from Genesis 6; the same advent that levels the mountains terrifies the ones who left their station. And Enoch says who comes and what for: *And behold! He cometh with ten thousands of His holy ones To execute judgement upon all, And to destroy all the ungodly: And to convict all flesh Of all the works of their ungodliness which they have ungodly committed, And of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against Him.* (1 Enoch 1:9). The judgement is upon all who broke the order they were given. The law that was broken stands, and the One who gave it is the One coming down.
note: old 37:7-9 was 1:5-7 under the wrong numbers, 1:9 reworded ("set-apart ones"); re-quoted from the live verses; Psalm 97:5 dropped (not in the index); canon kept

title: Peace with the righteous; the elect protected; light appears unto them
summary_md: The same advent that rends the earth turns to mercy for the chosen: *But with the righteous He will make peace. And will protect the elect, And mercy shall be upon them. And they shall all belong to Elohim (God), And they shall be prospered, And they shall all be blessed. And He will help them all, And light shall appear unto them, And He will make peace with them.* (1 Enoch 1:8). The light that appears to the elect is Isaiah's glory rising on the chosen people: *Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of Yahuah (LORD) is risen upon thee* (Isaiah 60:1). Their belonging to Elohim (God) comes before anything they do about it; they were chosen before they were called: *According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love* (Ephesians 1:4), and no charge can stand against them — *Who shall lay any thing to the charge of Elohim's (God's) elect? It is Elohim (God) that justifieth* (Romans 8:33). Within Enoch's own parables the same protected lot is named and saved: *And the wisdom of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath revealed him to the holy and righteous; For he hath preserved the lot of the righteous, Because they have hated and despised this world of unrighteousness, And have hated all its works and ways in the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits: For in his name they are saved, And according to his good pleasure hath it been in regard to their life.* (1 Enoch 48:7). These elect are a people kept and gathered, the righteous of both houses brought home, and the peace He makes with them is the other face of the judgement He brings on everyone else.
note: old 37:10 was 1:8 under the wrong number; re-cited; "the election the framework insists" removed; 48:7 stood and is quoted in full; canon kept

title: The light of the righteous shall shine
summary_md: The first parable opens on the day the two companies are parted: *The First Parable. When the congregation of the righteous shall appear, And sinners shall be judged for their sins, And shall be driven from the face of the earth: And when the Righteous One shall appear before the eyes of the righteous, Whose elect works hang upon Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And light shall appear to the righteous and the elect who dwell on the earth, Where then will be the dwelling of the sinners, And where the resting-place of those who have denied Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits? It had been good for them if they had not been born.* (1 Enoch 38:1-2). Then the light is given, and the mighty cannot look at it: *From that time those that possess the earth shall no longer be powerful and exalted: And they shall not be able to behold the face of the holy, For Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits has caused His light to appear On the face of the holy, righteous, and elect.* (1 Enoch 38:4). Daniel saw the same dawn: *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever* (Daniel 12:3). Yahusha (Jesus) said it plainly at the end of the wheat and the tares, the very seed-war Enoch's Watchers began: *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear* (Matthew 13:43). The Wisdom of Solomon carries the same hope for the persecuted elect: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). Notice where the light comes from in Enoch. Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits causes it to appear on their faces. The righteous here are a people kept in covenant and lit from outside themselves, and the shining is given, never earned.
note: old 38:1 and 38:8 were not the Charles words; the live 38:1-2 and 38:4 carry the parable and the light; canon kept

title: The Elect One sits on the throne of glory to judge
summary_md: Enoch names the One who judges: *And he shall judge the secret things, And none shall be able to utter a lying word before him; For he is the Elect One before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits according to His good pleasure.* (1 Enoch 49:4). In the second parable the throne is set under Him in so many words: *On that day Mine Elect One shall sit on the throne of glory And shall try their works, And their places of rest shall be innumerable. And their souls shall grow strong within them when they see Mine elect ones, And those who have called upon My glorious name:* (1 Enoch 45:3). This is a title, not a comparison. The Elect One is chosen and appointed by Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits and seated to judge, and Yahusha (Jesus) took up exactly this throne-language as His own: *When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory* (Matthew 25:31); and to the twelve, *in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Matthew 19:28), which is the gathered tribes being judged, not a church standing in for them. The Spirit that fits the Elect One to judge truly is the Spirit Isaiah foresaw on the Branch: *And the spirit of Yahuah (LORD) shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahuah (LORD)* (Isaiah 11:2), so that *with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth* (Isaiah 11:4). Enoch says the same of him in the verse before the judging: *And in him dwells the spirit of wisdom, And the spirit which gives insight, And the spirit of understanding and of might, And the spirit of those who have fallen asleep in righteousness.* (1 Enoch 49:3).
note: old 38:10 is a paraphrase of 49:4 from the corrupt text; rebuilt on 49:4 and 49:3 with 45:3 (which stood); canon kept

title: The Righteous One appears; the deeds of sinners revealed
summary_md: Before the throne is even set, Enoch names the One who appears: *And when the Righteous One shall appear before the eyes of the righteous, Whose elect works hang upon Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And light shall appear to the righteous and the elect who dwell on the earth, Where then will be the dwelling of the sinners, And where the resting-place of those who have denied Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits? It had been good for them if they had not been born.* (1 Enoch 38:2), and *When the secrets of the righteous shall be revealed and the sinners judged, And the godless driven from the presence of the righteous and elect,* (1 Enoch 38:3). This is the Messiah, the Righteous One in whom righteousness dwells. Isaiah names Him the Father's righteous servant: *He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities* (Isaiah 53:11). The congregation of the righteous that appears with Him is Isaiah's own gate-scene: *Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in* (Isaiah 26:2), a nation that keeps the truth, which is the covenant kept and not a curse escaped. Enoch's parables answer who this Righteous One is: *And he answered and said unto me: This is the Son of Adam who hath righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath chosen him, And whose lot hath the pre-eminence before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits in uprightness for ever.* (1 Enoch 46:3). He is chosen and named by the Head of Days before any mouth confesses Him. The choosing comes first, and the confession follows it.
note: old 38:3 was not the Charles words; the live 38:2-3 carry the Righteous One and the secrets revealed; 46:3 stood; canon kept

title: The kings and mighty cast down from their thrones
summary_md: Enoch turns to the powers of the earth: *From that time those that possess the earth shall no longer be powerful and exalted: And they shall not be able to behold the face of the holy, For Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits has caused His light to appear On the face of the holy, righteous, and elect. Then shall the kings and the mighty perish And be given into the hands of the righteous and holy. And thenceforward none shall seek for themselves mercy from Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits For their life is at an end.* (1 Enoch 38:4-6). Revelation shows the same panic of the mighty at the day of wrath: *And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains* (Revelation 6:15), crying *Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?* (Revelation 6:17). The furnace is Yahusha's (Jesus') own word for the end of the tares: *And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth* (Matthew 13:42). And Enoch's parables name who does the overthrowing: *And this Son of Adam whom thou hast seen Shall raise up the kings and the mighty from their seats, [And the strong from their thrones] And shall loosen the reins of the strong, And break the teeth of the sinners.* (1 Enoch 46:4). The judgement here is on those who possess the earth and will not acknowledge where their kingdom came from. It is the systems of oppression that are broken, and the people under them are the ones being set free.
note: old 38:6 (furnace of fire) is not in Charles 38; the live 38:4-6 carry the fall of the kings; 62:9 was really 46:4 and is quoted there; canon kept

title: Those who led the world astray bound with chains
summary_md: The first parable asks where the sinners will find a resting-place once the Righteous One appears: *And when the Righteous One shall appear before the eyes of the righteous, Whose elect works hang upon Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And light shall appear to the righteous and the elect who dwell on the earth, Where then will be the dwelling of the sinners, And where the resting-place of those who have denied Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits? It had been good for them if they had not been born.* (1 Enoch 38:2). The third parable answers it: *And he sat on the throne of his glory, And the sum of judgement was given unto the Son of Adam, And he caused the sinners to pass away and be destroyed from off the face of the earth, And those who have led the world astray. With chains shall they be bound, And in their assemblage-place of destruction shall they be imprisoned, And all their works vanish from the face of the earth.* (1 Enoch 69:27-28). The deeds of sinners are revealed before the throne, and that is the scene John saw at the books opened: *And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away* (Revelation 20:11), and *I saw the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God); and the books were opened... and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works* (Revelation 20:12). The waking to that twofold verdict is Daniel's: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt* (Daniel 12:2). The chains are the Watchers' own chains carried forward to the ones who learned from them: *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day* (Jude 1:6). The Creator's order is restored against the rebellion that led the world astray, and the Son of Adam is the one seated to do it.
note: old 38:2 and 38:12 ran 69:27-28 words under chapter 38 numbers; rebuilt on the live 38:2 and 69:27-28; Jude 1:6 added from the verse index; canon kept

title: The dwelling-places of the righteous and the elect
summary_md: Enoch's spirit is carried off and set down where the holy live: *And in those days a whirlwind carried me off from the earth, And set me down at the end of the heavens. And there I saw another vision, the dwelling-places of the holy, And the resting-places of the righteous.* (1 Enoch 39:3-4), and *Here mine eyes saw their dwellings with His righteous angels, And their resting-places with the holy. And they petitioned and interceded and prayed for the children of men, And righteousness flowed before them as water, And mercy like dew upon the earth: Thus it is amongst them for ever and ever.* (1 Enoch 39:5). He longs for the place: *There I wished to dwell, And my spirit longed for that dwelling-place: And there heretofore hath been my portion, For so has it been established concerning me before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 39:8). This is the hope Yahusha (Jesus) names to His own — *In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.* (John 14:2) — and the scene John is shown at the throne: *Therefore are they before the throne of Elohim (God), and serve him day and night in his temple: and he that sitteth on the throne shall dwell among them.* (Revelation 7:15). The promise is not escape but dwelling-with. Enoch says the righteous and elect stand without number before the Elect One for ever, and John hears the same thing proclaimed over the renewed earth: *Behold, the tabernacle of Elohim (God) is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people* (Revelation 21:3). Enoch's portion in that place was established before he ever saw it, and that is how it is for all the elect: the dwelling is prepared for them before they arrive.
note: old 39:3 and 39:6 were not the Charles words; the live 39:3-5 and 39:8 carry the dwellings; canon kept

title: The Elect One seen in the dwelling of the holy
summary_md: Among the dwelling-places of the holy Enoch sees the One they gather around: *And in that place mine eyes saw the Elect One of righteousness and of faith, And righteousness shall prevail in his days, And the righteous and elect shall be without number before Him for ever and ever. And I saw his dwelling-place under the wings of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits. And all the righteous and elect before Him shall be strong as fiery lights, And their mouth shall be full of blessing, And their lips extol the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And righteousness before Him shall never fail, [And uprightness shall never fail before Him.]* (1 Enoch 39:6-7). He is the Elect One of righteousness and of faith, and his dwelling is under the wings of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, ordered under the Father and set before the righteous at the same time. Isaiah names this same chosen One: *Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles.* (Isaiah 42:1). When Yahusha (Jesus) takes up the title in the flesh, He sets the throne of glory at the centre of the judgement: *When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:* (Matthew 25:31). Enoch names the Elect One where Daniel only sees *one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days* (Daniel 7:13). Daniel is watching a figure who looks like a mortal man because He took on flesh; Enoch is standing in front of the same One before He did, and the righteous around Him are already strong as fiery lights. He is the chosen One, named before any tongue could call on Him.
note: old 39:5 (voice of the Elect One from the throne) is not in Charles 39; the live 39:6-7 carry the Elect One in the dwelling of the holy; title changed to fit; canon kept

title: Righteousness flowing before them like water
summary_md: Of the resting-places of the holy Enoch says: *Here mine eyes saw their dwellings with His righteous angels, And their resting-places with the holy. And they petitioned and interceded and prayed for the children of men, And righteousness flowed before them as water, And mercy like dew upon the earth: Thus it is amongst them for ever and ever.* (1 Enoch 39:5). The prophet pleads for exactly this outpouring against a crooked generation: *But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.* (Amos 5:24). And the image finds its source at the throne John is shown, where the river of life comes out from the Father and the Lamb: *And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of Elohim (God) and of the Lamb.* (Revelation 22:1). Within Enoch's own parables the source is named: *And in that place I saw the fountain of righteousness Which was inexhaustible: And around it were many fountains of wisdom: And all the thirsty drank of them, And were filled with wisdom, And their dwellings were with the righteous and holy and elect.* (1 Enoch 48:1). So the righteousness that flows like water before the holy is not something they make. It draws from a fountain that does not run dry, and they carry it as intercession for the children of men. Righteousness here is a gift flowing out and mercy coming down like dew, and the holy do not keep it to themselves.
note: mechanical draft had a broken lead ("they *Here mine eyes…"); re-cited to 39:5 and the lead sentence mended; 48:1 quoted in full
